The monitor’s contrast setting is too high.
explanation: The most likely causes are that no device (such as a video card) is sending video or that the source cable has been disconnected. Check the connections on both ends, and make sure the computer, the video source, is on and booting properly.
whyWrong: Even with the brightness at 0, most monitors still show the image.
The OSD is visible, so the monitor's backlight is working.
A maximum contrast setting still leaves an image on the screen.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 34

stem: You are a technician working on a problem with a projector. While investigating, you find that the lamp turns off for brief periods during longer demonstrations. You replace the lamp, but the problem continues, and now you get a message that appears just before the lamp turns off. Which of the following should you perform? (Select the two best answers.)
explanation: A lamp that turns off during long demonstrations most likely points to overheating: the projector shuts the lamp off until it cools down, so the cooling fan may have failed and need replacing. The message that appears is most likely asking you to reset the lamp life counter to zero, because the projector detects a new lamp.
whyWrong: The video resolution does not affect how hot the projector gets.
A more powerful lamp might not work in the projector and would create more heat.
Adjusting the brightness does not fix a failed cooling fan.
The laptop's video driver has no effect on the projector lamp overheating.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 69

stem: A user complains that icons and text on a new 4K monitor appear too small, making them difficult to read. Which of the following is the BEST solution to this problem?
options: Decrease the refresh rate in the monitor's OSD menu.
Change the monitor's color depth to 16-bit.
Increase the display scaling percentage in the operating system.
explanation: On high-resolution monitors such as 4K displays, text and icons can look too small because of the high pixel density. Increasing the display scaling percentage in the operating system enlarges these elements without lowering the resolution, so content stays sharp and properly proportioned.
whyWrong: The refresh rate controls how often the image is redrawn, not the size of text and icons.
A 16-bit color depth lowers image quality and color range without changing the size of on-screen elements.
Lowering the resolution to 1024×768 enlarges text but makes the 4K image blurry and stretched.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 85

stem: If the video on your laptop is not working, what should you do to troubleshoot it? (Choose two.)
options: Remove the display unit and reattach it.
Power the system off and back on.
explanation: Two helpful things to try are toggling the video output function key (usually something like Fn+F8) and plugging an external monitor into the laptop. The function key may have sent the output to an external display, and an external monitor shows whether the video adapter works.
whyWrong: Removing the display is possible but not necessary until simpler checks are done.
Powering the system off and back on isn't likely to correct the problem.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 1

stem: The display on a laptop computer is continuously flickering. Which of the following are MOST LIKELY to cause this problem? (Choose two.)
explanation: Perpetually dim or flickering screens are most likely caused by a failing backlight or inverter, which supplies power to the backlight. When the backlight's power is unstable, the whole image flickers.
whyWrong: A failing display panel more often shows dead pixels or distortion than a constant flicker.
LCD devices are not subject to interference from fans.
An incorrect video driver is not a likely cause of a flickering laptop screen.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 5

stem: You are having problems with the video card in one of your computers. Where should you check for troubleshooting information?
options: Another computer with the same video card
The manual that came with the card
explanation: The manufacturer's website is the first place you should go for information on your products, including troubleshooting information. Many years ago, manufacturers would provide paper manuals with their products, but that's almost unheard of today, unless you download a PDF version from the website.
whyWrong: Another computer with the same card can help test the card but is not a source of troubleshooting information.
Paper manuals rarely ship with video cards today, and they are not kept up to date.
Server logs can show error codes, but they won't tell you how to fix anything.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 6

stem: The display on your laptop appears warped and fuzzy. You plug in an external monitor, and the image on it is fine. What is the MOST LIKELY cause of the problem?
explanation: It has to be a problem with the LCD display. If it were the video card, the display would appear warped and fuzzy on the external monitor as well.
whyWrong: A faulty video card would distort the image on the external monitor as well.
Many motherboards contain video circuitry, but a fault there would also affect the external monitor.
A corrupted video driver would cause the same problem on all displays.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 8

stem: You are connecting a laptop to a conference room's A/V system for a presentation using an HDMI cable. Your screen image appears on the displays, but when you play a video, there is no audio. When you unplug from the A/V system, the audio plays on your laptop. What should you do NEXT?
options: Use a DVI cable instead of an HDMI cable.
Reboot the laptop and reconnect to the A/V system.
Check the audio output settings on the laptop.
Restart the A/V system and reconnect to the laptop.
explanation: If the video works but the audio doesn't, it's probably a settings issue. Either the audio output is set incorrectly, or the volume is turned down or muted. Check those things first.
whyWrong: HDMI cables carry audio but DVI cables do not, so switching to DVI would make it worse.
Rebooting the laptop probably isn't necessary when the problem is an audio setting.
Restarting the A/V system probably isn't necessary when the problem is an audio setting on the laptop.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 16

stem: An office has a flat-screen monitor in the lobby that displays information for visitors. Recently, an employee changed the material in the slide that's always shown. Even though the new slide can be seen, the old slide material still appears faintly on the screen. What is the solution to the problem?
options: Shut down and restart the monitor.
Shut down the presentation software. Reopen it, delete the old slide completely, and then restart presentation mode.
explanation: The symptom here is a display burn-in, also known as a ghost image. The only solution is to replace the monitor. Burn-in happens when the same static image is shown for a long time and leaves a permanent mark on the panel.
whyWrong: Restarting the monitor does not remove an image that is burned into the panel.
The old slide is burned into the screen itself, so changing the presentation software will not remove it.
Degaussing applied to old CRT monitors and does nothing for a flat-screen panel.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 18

stem: The video projector mounted to the ceiling in a conference room periodically shuts down during the middle of presentations without warning. When it shuts down, it won't power back on for about an hour. What should you check for?
options: Ensure that the proper mounting bracket was used for the projector.
Look for dust buildup in the projector's air filter.
Ensure that the input source is set correctly.
Look at the display settings to change the auto power-off time setting.
explanation: The projector is probably shutting off because it's overheating, and that can be caused by dust buildup in the air filter. Check that first, but preferably not when the projector is hot. The long wait before it powers back on fits a thermal shutdown.
whyWrong: The mounting bracket has nothing to do with shutdowns unless it covers the air intake.
The input source has nothing to do with the projector shutting down and refusing to power back on.
Auto power-off normally acts only after a period of inactivity, not in the middle of a presentation.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 20

stem: A company executive calls complaining that the projector mounted on the ceiling of the conference room suddenly cut off in the middle of her presentation to the board. You go to check it out while the room is not in use, but it seems to work fine. Which of the following is MOST LIKELY?
options: The projector went to sleep because she forgot to configure her OS to extend the desktop to the projector.
The projector overheated and shut down because the fan stopped working or its filter is clogged.
explanation: Since the projector worked when you tried it, the lamp did not go out. It is possible the power cord wiggled loose, but the fact that the projector is mounted on the ceiling makes that unlikely. The projector probably did not go to sleep while she was actively presenting. If a projector overheats because of a dead fan or clogged filter, it shuts down to protect itself.
whyWrong: A ceiling-mounted projector's cord is rarely disturbed, so a loose cord is unlikely.
A burnt-out lamp would not work again when you test it later.
An active presentation keeps the projector awake, and desktop settings do not make a projector sleep.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 17: Display Technologies, Chapter Review question 9

stem: Rafael gets a tech call from a user with a brand new laptop complaining that his display is flickering. What is the MOST LIKELY issue?
options: The laptop uses a plasma display.
The laptop uses a CRT display.
The laptop display drivers are outdated.
The laptop display is faulty and needs to be replaced.
explanation: Flicker is most commonly caused by software issues like outdated or corrupted display drivers. On a brand new laptop, the hardware is unlikely to be faulty, so update the drivers first.
whyWrong: Laptops do not use plasma displays.
Laptops do not use CRT displays.
A hardware fault is unlikely on a brand new laptop; check software causes first.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 23: Portable Computing, Chapter Review question 10

stem: A user is having trouble reading the screen on their legacy LCD monitor. The screen looks very dim. What do you think is MOST LIKELY causing the problem?
options: The brightness has been turned down
explanation: An LCD monitor gets its brightness from a backlight, so when the backlight fails, the image is very dim or even black. Turning up the brightness setting does not help if the backlight itself is failing.
whyWrong: The brightness setting is the first thing a user would try, and a failing backlight stays dim even at full brightness.
A legacy LCD monitor is not a touchscreen, so it has no digitizer.
A damaged VGA cable gives no image or a distorted image with wrong colors, not a uniformly dim one.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.2 question 7
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.2; dim image is a current 5.3 symptom.

stem: A system administrator has determined that a user’s laptop has the wrong screen resolution. They believe that a recent Windows update has caused the problem. What stage in the troubleshooting process have they just carried out?
options: Establishing a theory of probable cause
Testing the theory to determine the cause
explanation: The administrator has just established a theory of probable cause: they think a recent Windows update caused the wrong screen resolution. The next stage is to test the theory, followed by establishing a plan of action.
whyWrong: The problem was already identified when the administrator found the wrong screen resolution.
A plan of action comes only after the theory has been tested and the cause confirmed.
Testing the theory is the stage after this one; the administrator has not tested anything yet.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.1 question 5
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.1 (troubleshooting methodology). In 220-1201 the methodology is listed before Domain 5 as a best practice, not a numbered objective; tagged by the device in the question.

stem: A technician has been called to a classroom as the projector is very dim. Which of the following is causing the problem?
options: They need to adjust the display settings
explanation: A projector bulb has a limited lifespan, and as it nears the end of its life it becomes dim. When it fails completely, you may hear a pop and the image disappears.
whyWrong: An inverter powers the backlight of some LCD screens, not a projector bulb.
Display settings change the resolution and layout, but they cannot make a worn bulb brighter.
A digitizer handles touch input on a touch screen and has nothing to do with projector brightness.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.4 question 1
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.4 (video, projector, display) = current 5.3.

stem: A technician is setting up a projector in a conference room and gets an error saying “no signal.” What could be the cause of this issue?
options: The cable to the projector is faulty and needs to be replaced
The projectors’ bulb needs to be replaced
The computer needs to have its display set to “extend this display”
explanation: If the projector shows a “no signal” error, either the cable is not connected properly or it is faulty and needs to be replaced. Check that the projector is set to the correct input source as well.
whyWrong: A failing bulb gives a dim or no image, but the projector could not show a “no signal” message without light.
A broken laptop monitor does not stop the video output from reaching the projector.
Changing to “extend this display” does not help while the projector receives no signal at all.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.4 question 2
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.4 (video, projector, display) = current 5.3.

stem: A professor at a university connects their laptop to the projector in a theatre. The image being projected is fuzzy. Which of the following is causing this issue?
options: The laptop display setting needs to be adjusted
The projector lens needs to be adjusted
The projector bulb needs to be replaced
explanation: If a projector shows a fuzzy image, adjust the lens focus until the picture is sharp. A defective cable gives a “no signal” error or distortion instead.
whyWrong: A defective cable usually gives no signal or a distorted image, not a picture that is evenly out of focus.
The laptop display settings change resolution and layout, not the focus of the projector lens.
A worn projector bulb makes the image dim, not fuzzy.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.4 question 3
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.4 (video, projector, display) = current 5.3.

stem: A presenter is trying to play a video that is on a DVD in their laptop. They can hear the sound but get an error on the projector stating “COPY PROTECTION: THE DVI/HDMI OUTPUT IS BLOCKED.” Which of the following is causing this issue?
options: The display settings need to be adjusted
There is a problem with the DVD player
explanation: High-bandwidth Digital Content Protection (HDCP) lets a content source such as a DVD or Blu-ray disc block its output when the display devices do not support HDCP and cannot authenticate with it. The projector here is not HDCP-compatible, so the video is blocked while the sound still plays.
whyWrong: A faulty HDMI cable would give a “no signal” error, not an HDCP message.
The projector already receives output, so the display settings are not the problem.
If the DVD player had a problem, there would be no sound either.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.4 question 4
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.4 (video, projector, display) = current 5.3. Book option 'protector' corrected to 'projector'.

stem: A computer technician has connected a laptop to a projector in a lecture hall but an image is not being projected on the screen. They go back to their workshop and bring cables that they know are working. After swapping the cables, they get a “no source found” error. What should the computer technician do NEXT? (Choose two.)
options: Check the connection on the HDMI cable
Run displayswitch.exe and select either duplicate or extend
Go to display settings on the laptop, choose multiple displays, and duplicate these displays
explanation: A “no source found” error with known good cables means that the laptop is not sending its image to the projector. Run displayswitch.exe (Windows key+P) and select Duplicate or Extend, or go to the laptop display settings, choose multiple displays, and duplicate the displays.
whyWrong: The projector is showing error messages, so its bulb is working.
The cables have just been replaced with known good ones, so the HDMI connection is not the cause.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.4 question 5
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.4 (video, projector, display) = current 5.3.

stem: A new TV and video soundbar system has just been set up in a boardroom. The TV is being used to play videos from a presentation laptop. Sound is coming from the laptop and from the TV but the video soundbar is not producing any audio. Which of the following is causing the problem?
options: The soundbar is not turned on
The soundbar volume is too low
The High-Definition Multimedia Interface-Audio Return Channel (HDMI-ARC) port on the TV is not connected to the soundbar
The video resolution is too low
explanation: HDMI Audio Return Channel (HDMI-ARC) sends the audio from the TV to an external sound system over the HDMI cable. If the soundbar is not connected to the TV’s ARC port, it receives no audio from the TV.
whyWrong: The soundbar was just set up for the meeting, and a soundbar with no power is less likely than a wrong connection.
A low volume would still give some sound; the soundbar produces no audio at all.
Video resolution affects the picture, not whether audio reaches the soundbar.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.4 question 7
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.4 (video, projector, display) = current 5.3.

stem: A user has called the help desk as their monitor is showing a purple tinge. Which of the following is MOST LIKELY causing the problem?
explanation: When a monitor shows a pink or purple tint over the whole screen, a faulty or loose video cable is the most likely cause, because one of the color signals is missing. Reseat or replace the cable first.
whyWrong: Display burn-in shows a ghost of a previous image, not a color tint over the whole screen.
A faulty graphics card more often gives artifacts or a flickering or blank screen, and it is less likely than a cable.
A burned-out bulb or backlight makes the screen dim or dark, not purple.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.4 question 8
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.4 (video, projector, display) = current 5.3.

stem: A computer technician has been called out to a conference room where the projector is intermittently rebooting. What will the computer technician do NEXT? (Choose two.)
options: Check the vents are dust-free and that there are no obstructions
Check that the projector fan is working properly
Check that the projector can handle the display resolution
explanation: A projector that shuts down or reboots intermittently is usually overheating. Check that the fans are working and that the vents and air filters are free from dust and obstructions.
whyWrong: You might check that the power cable is plugged in firmly, but replacing it is not the next step for an overheating projector.
The display resolution does not make a projector reboot.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.4 question 10
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.4 (video, projector, display) = current 5.3.

stem: The plasma screen in a conference room is displaying an image for about 60 seconds after it is shown on the screen. The presenter is using a presentation that is stored on their laptop via an HDMI cable. Which of the following is causing this issue?
explanation: Display burn-in (image retention) is where a previous image remains on the screen as a ghost image. Plasma screens are prone to it when the same image is shown for a long time.
whyWrong: Dead pixels are fixed dots that stay black or one color; they do not show a previous image.
A faulty cable causes flicker, color problems, or no signal, not a lingering previous image.
If the laptop froze, the same image would stay on both screens rather than fading on the plasma screen alone.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.4 question 11
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.4 (video, projector, display) = current 5.3.

stem: What is the primary purpose of testing the output resolution in a system?
options: To verify compatibility with different display devices
explanation: Testing the output resolution confirms that the system’s output works with different display devices, which can have different resolutions and capabilities. It helps avoid sizing issues such as distorted images or cut-off content.
whyWrong: Color accuracy is set by calibration and color settings, which is a secondary concern of a resolution test.
Image quality may improve with the right resolution, but the main purpose of the test is compatibility.
Testing the resolution does not make the system run faster.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.4 question 12
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.4 (video, projector, display) = current 5.3.

stem: Why does a projector power down unexpectedly during operation?
options: Overheating caused by a dirty air filter
Insufficient power supply to the projector
A malfunctioning lamp in the projector
A loose connection between the projector and power source
explanation: A dirty air filter restricts the airflow, so the projector overheats. To prevent damage, projectors power down automatically when they overheat.
whyWrong: An insufficient power supply would stop the projector from starting, not shut it down during use.
A failing lamp makes the image dim or dark, but it is not the usual cause of unexpected power-downs.
A loose power connection is possible, but overheating from a dirty filter is the common cause of shutdowns during use.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.6 question 9
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.6 (printers). The question is about a projector; tagged to current 5.3 intermittent projector shutdown.

stem: A user’s mobile device is overheating. Which of the following could be the problem? (Select the two best answers.)
options: The brightness setting is too low.
The device is not in a case.
explanation: A damaged battery and excessive gaming are the likely causes of overheating. Games keep the processor and display working hard, and a damaged battery can heat up and is a safety hazard.
whyWrong: A low brightness setting uses less power, so the device should run cooler.
A device without a case should not overheat, although a poorly made case could trap heat.
A defective charging cable usually does not make a device overheat; it likely does not charge the device at all.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 26: Troubleshooting Mobile Devices, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: You are troubleshooting a user’s smartphone. The user is unable to see anything on the screen. Of the following, what should you do FIRST?
options: Disassemble the device for proper reassembly.
explanation: Check the brightness slider first; the brightness might be turned all the way down, so in a bright place the screen looks blank. The device might also just need to be woken with the side button, the home button, or a double tap on the screen. If these steps fail, restart the device.
whyWrong: Do not open the device until every other option is exhausted, and only if you are qualified to work on it.
The volume mixer sliders control sound, not the display.
Screen calibration affects touch accuracy, not brightness.
Restarting comes after the quick brightness and wake checks fail.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 26: Troubleshooting Mobile Devices, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: When disassembling a mobile device, what should you not do?
options: Store screws in a logical manner.
explanation: Stay away from magnetically charged tools such as screwdrivers and bits, because they can potentially damage circuitry and components. Documenting, organizing screws, using manuals, following antistatic procedures, and labeling cables are all good practices when you work on mobile devices and computers.
whyWrong: Documenting what you see is a good practice that makes reassembly easier.
Storing screws in a logical order is a good practice, because mobile devices use many different screws.
Manufacturer manuals and service guides help you take the device apart correctly.
Antistatic procedures protect the device's components from electrostatic discharge.
Labeling cables helps you reconnect each one to the right place.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 26: Troubleshooting Mobile Devices, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: Which of the following are common reasons that a mobile device might not charge properly? (Select three.)
options: A cable is ripped or bent.
explanation: The charging cable is the first thing to check: inspect it for rips, bends, cuts, or a damaged connector. Check the device's charging port for dust and debris, and clear it with compressed air. If a port is damaged, the entire device probably needs to be repaired or replaced.
whyWrong: Airplane mode conserves battery power and does not normally affect charging.
Installing an app usually does not affect charging, although games can drain the battery quickly.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 26: Troubleshooting Mobile Devices, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: What can cause a digitizer to become nonresponsive? (Select three.)
explanation: A digitizer can become nonresponsive because of an application or OS failure, a frozen system, a loose display connection, a failed display, or user error. For example, gloves can prevent proper touchscreen response.
whyWrong: A bad charging cable affects charging, not the digitizer's response to touch.
Disabled audio affects sound only and has no effect on touch input.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 26: Troubleshooting Mobile Devices, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: A user reports that their smartphone has become noticeably slower when launching apps and navigating menus. Which of the following is the most appropriate FIRST step to troubleshoot this degraded performance?
options: Update all apps to the latest versions.
Perform a factory reset of the device.
Clear the system cache partition from recovery mode.
explanation: Closing background apps is the recommended first step for degraded performance, because it quickly frees system memory and reduces CPU load. Updating apps, clearing the cache, or a factory reset may help in some cases, but those steps are secondary or more drastic. Start with the least invasive option that targets common causes of slowdowns.
whyWrong: Updating all apps can help over time, but it is not a targeted first fix and adds background activity while it runs.
A factory reset erases all data and settings and is a last resort.
Clearing the system cache partition from recovery mode is an advanced step that is needed less often.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 86

stem: A user complains that his mouse cursor randomly jumps to different places on the screen when he types. Which device might you want to disable to prevent this from happening?
explanation: The trackpad sits below the keyboard, where a user's palms may rest when he is typing. That contact may cause the mouse cursor to appear to jump on the screen. Disabling the touchpad should prevent this from happening.
whyWrong: An external mouse is not touched while typing, so it does not make the cursor jump.
A point stick sits in the middle of the keyboard but is not brushed by resting palms.
A trackball is rarely built into laptops and is not touched by the palms while typing.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware, Review Questions question 4
note: Earlier in Docter chapter 4 (220-1201 1.x); tagged with 5.4 cursor drift/touch calibration.

stem: A user complains that his 2-in-1 laptop screen does not properly detect where he places his finger on the screen. What should you do FIRST to resolve the issue?
explanation: If the touchscreen is not responding properly, the first step is to recalibrate it. If it continues to have problems, the screen may be defective and might need to be replaced.
whyWrong: Replacing the touchscreen comes only after recalibration fails to fix it.
The trackpad is not involved when the touchscreen misreads finger positions.
Recalibrating the trackpad does not affect where the touchscreen registers touches.
Degaussing is a process used on old CRT monitors and is not relevant to touchscreens.
Degaussing applied to CRT monitors and has nothing to do with a trackpad.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware, Review Questions question 7
note: Earlier in Docter chapter 4 (220-1201 1.x); tagged with 5.4 cursor drift/touch calibration.

stem: A user tells you that his Android phone case is bulging, and the device has been hot to the touch lately. You suspect a swollen battery. Which of the following is a good NEXT step?
options: Leave the device on to drain the battery, and then recharge the device.
Turn the device off, let it cool to room temperature, and then recharge the device.
explanation: With a swollen battery, the best solution is to replace the device. If you are experienced with mobile device batteries, you may be able to replace the battery, but be careful. You should not charge a swollen battery or freeze the system.
whyWrong: A swollen battery should not be drained and recharged, because charging it can make it rupture or catch fire.
Cooling the phone does not fix a swollen battery, and recharging it is unsafe.
A battery calibration utility only corrects the charge reading and does nothing for a swollen battery.
Freezing the device does not repair a swollen battery and can damage the phone.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 3

stem: A user brings in an iPhone and the touchscreen is not responding. What should you try FIRST to get the device functioning again?
options: Hold the power button and the sleep/wake button for 10 seconds to reset the device.
Restore the device to factory settings.
Replace the battery in the device.
Hold the power button for 10 seconds to force the device to power off.
explanation: The first step should be to try to reboot the device. In most cases with a frozen smartphone, holding the power button down for about 10 seconds will force it to power off. If that doesn't work, then you can try a forced reset with the device's button combination.
whyWrong: A forced reset with a button combination is the step to try after a simple forced power-off fails.
Restoring factory settings erases the device and is not needed yet.
Replacing the battery is not needed for a screen that is frozen.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 12
note: Button sequences differ between iPhone models; the book's point is that a restart comes before a reset or restore.

stem: The stylus for your manager's tablet has stopped working. The tablet responds to input when you touch the screen with your finger. Which troubleshooting steps should you try NEXT? (Choose three.)
options: Replace the battery in the stylus.
Replace the tip of the stylus.
Replace the stylus sensor in the tablet.
Shut down and restart the tablet.
explanation: If the tablet seems to be performing normally but the stylus appears to be the problem, focus there. Many styluses have batteries that can go bad, or it's possible the tip has gone bad as well. Rebooting is almost always a good option too.
whyWrong: There is no stylus sensor in tablets; the screen digitizer picks up the stylus signal.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 13

stem: You are unable to charge an Android smartphone. You tried a second charger that is known to work, and the phone will still not charge. What should you do NEXT?
options: Use the secondary auxiliary port to charge the smartphone.
Use a DC charger instead of an AC charger.
explanation: If the charger works, what about the outlet? If the phone refuses to charge with either charger or outlet, try restarting the device. If it still won't charge, it could have a problem with the battery or the charging port.
whyWrong: Replacing the phone is premature before you rule out the power outlet.
Android phones do not have a secondary auxiliary port for charging.
Whether the charger draws AC or DC power makes no difference here.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 15

stem: Clara just finished a long road trip on a hot day in a car with a broken air conditioner. When she arrives at her destination, she immediately opens her laptop, which was working before she left, to check her e-mails. For some reason, every time she tries to power up the computer, it shuts down again within a few seconds. What is the MOST LIKELY problem?
options: The laptop’s hard drive died and needs to be replaced.
The laptop display is faulty and needs to be replaced.
The laptop fans are very dusty and need to be cleaned.
The laptop is already hot from sitting in the car and needs time to cool off.
explanation: Because Clara just had a long road trip in a hot car, the laptop is most likely already hot and needs time to cool off. A laptop shuts itself down when it detects overheating to protect its components.
whyWrong: A dead hard drive would cause boot errors, not a shutdown seconds after power-on.
A faulty display would show no image, but the laptop would stay powered on.
Dusty fans build up over time, but the laptop worked fine before the trip.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 23: Portable Computing, Chapter Review question 4

stem: Which of the following would be a legitimate reason a mobile device is running slowly?
explanation: Lack of storage space is a legitimate reason a mobile device runs slowly. With little free storage, the OS has no room for temporary files and caches.
whyWrong: Incorrect calibration makes touches register in the wrong spot, not slow performance.
Mobile device RAM is fixed by the hardware design and is not too slow for the device.
An incorrect app version affects that app, not the whole device's speed.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 25: Maintaining and Securing Mobile Devices, Chapter Review question 2

stem: Joyce notices her GPS map app gives the error “GPS coordinates not available.” What should she try FIRST?
options: Stop and start GPS on the mobile device.
Move to a place where she can get a good GPS signal.
explanation: Joyce needs to move to a place where she can get a good GPS signal. GPS needs a clear view of the sky, so buildings, tunnels, and trees can block the satellite signals.
whyWrong: Another app uses the same GPS receiver and would have the same lack of signal.
Restarting GPS does not help when the satellite signal is blocked.
A firmware update is a later step and does not fix a blocked signal.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 25: Maintaining and Securing Mobile Devices, Chapter Review question 3
note: All-in-One 11e (220-1101/1102) Ch. 25: closest symptom is Poor/no connectivity; location services are 220-1201 1.3.

stem: A user’s laptop is working perfectly fine, but for some reason, when they attempt to use it in a coffee shop, it will not power up. The user confirms that the battery is plugged in but notices a small bump on the battery. Which of the following is the MOST LIKELY cause of this problem?
options: The system fan is not working
The battery has failed, as it is defective and needs replacing
explanation: At work, the laptop is plugged into the mains and runs on AC power, but in the coffee shop it must run on its battery. The bump on the battery shows that it is swollen, which means it has failed and must be replaced. A swollen battery is also a safety hazard, so stop using it.
whyWrong: The laptop works when it is plugged in, so the power adapter is unlikely to be faulty.
A corrupt operating system would still let the laptop power up, then fail during boot.
A failed system fan would cause overheating and crashes, not stop the laptop from powering up.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.1 question 3
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.1 (laptop hardware); swollen battery is a current 5.4 symptom.

stem: A user has put their phone on charging, but the battery is draining quickly and is recharging very slowly. The phone is also hot to the touch. What is wrong with the phone?
options: The battery needs to be replaced
The battery is set to low power mode
explanation: When a battery reaches the end of its life, it does not fully charge and does not hold a charge for long. It also tends to overheat. The battery needs to be replaced.
whyWrong: A faulty charging cable would give no charge at all, and it would not make the phone hot.
The digitizer is the touch layer of the screen, and a broken one would not make the phone hot or drain the battery.
Low power mode uses less power, so the phone would run cooler and the battery would last longer.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.1 question 7
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.1; poor battery health and overheating are current 5.4 symptoms.

stem: John Smith plugged his iPhone into his bedside power socket prior to going to bed, but in the morning, the battery displays a 5% charge. He then goes to breakfast, boils the kettle for a cup of tea, and plugs the phone’s charger into the kettle’s socket. After 30 minutes, the phone still does not seem to be charging. The phone charger is not approved by Apple. Which of the following steps should he take FIRST to investigate the issue?
options: Reset the phone to factory settings
Check the power rating of the charger
Set the battery to low power mode
explanation: He should first check the power rating of the charger. A charger that is not approved for the phone may supply too little power to charge it, which is the most probable cause here.
whyWrong: Deleting apps reduces the resources the phone uses, but it does not affect whether it charges.
A factory reset will not fix a charging problem caused by the charger.
Low power mode saves battery once the phone has charge, but it does not make the phone charge.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.1 question 12
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.1; improper charging is a current 5.4 symptom.

stem: A lawyer left court carrying a large number of case files. They tripped and accidentally dropped some of their files along with their mobile phone that was resting on top. When the lawyer picked up the phone, the screen did not appear broken, but 10 minutes later, when they attempted to send an email from the phone, the mail icon was unresponsive. The same was true for every other app they attempted to access. What do you think happened?
explanation: The digitizer is the layer over the phone screen that makes the touchscreen work. When the icons display normally but do not respond to touch, the digitizer is most likely broken and must be replaced.
whyWrong: With no power, the screen would be black and no icons would display.
A CPU problem would make apps slow or crash, not stop every touch from registering.
Not every listed cause applies, because the screen has power and displays normally.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.2 question 15
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.2; digitizer issues are a current 5.4 symptom.

stem: A user is finding it difficult to plug their phone charger into their cell phone, and so orders a new charger from Amazon. However, when the new charger is inserted, the same thing happens. It does not seem to fit. Which of the following is the cause and solution of the issue?
options: The port that the user is plugging the cable into has a build-up of lint, and they need to use compressed air to clear it
The port that the user is plugging the cable into has a build-up of lint, and they need to blow into the port to clear it
The port that the user is plugging the cable into has a build-up of lint, and they need to spray WD-40 into the port to clear it
The port that the user is plugging the cable into has a build-up of lint, and they need to use a long darning needle to clear it
explanation: When a cable cannot be fully inserted into a charging port, the most likely reason is lint or another foreign object lodged in the port. The best way to clear it is a blast of compressed air; a non-metal tool such as a toothpick can also work.
whyWrong: Blowing into the port adds moisture from your breath, which can damage the electrical components.
WD-40 is a liquid that is an electrical hazard on components and leaves an oily residue.
A metal needle can short-circuit the port contacts and damage the phone.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.3 question 4
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.3 (mobile accessories and ports); improper charging and damaged ports are current 5.4 symptoms.

stem: When using a tablet with a touch pen, you get erroneous behavior such as an erratically moving cursor. Which of the following are the FIRST three steps you should take to identify the problem? (Choose three.)
options: Check whether the screen is damaged
explanation: When a touchscreen behaves erratically, first check that the screen is not damaged. Then check that it is clean, and then recalibrate the touch pen and screen.
whyWrong: A low touch pen battery makes the pen stop responding; it does not make the cursor move erratically.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.3 question 9
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.3; cursor drift/touch calibration is a current 5.4 symptom.

stem: A member of the sales team contacts the support desk to say that their cell phone is overheating. Which of the following is causing this to happen? (Choose three.)
options: Using the phone as a Wi-Fi hotspot
Several outdated applications being left open
explanation: A phone gets hot when it works hard, for example as a Wi-Fi hotspot for a long time. Phones also overheat when the battery is near the end of its life, which also makes it charge poorly and drain quickly. Many apps left open, especially outdated ones, make the CPU work harder and raise the temperature.
whyWrong: A cracked screen may stop the touchscreen responding, but it does not make the phone hot.
A cheap charging cable may charge slowly or not at all, but it does not make the phone overheat.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.3 question 17
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.3; overheating is a current 5.4 symptom.

stem: A user has a problem with their laptop and a second-line support technician has arrived. The support technician knows that they must try and identify the problem. Which of the following should the support technician do? (Choose two.)
options: Back up all of the data
Ask the user whether they made any recent changes
Ask the user what they were doing before the incident occurred
Search the vendor’s website for guidance
explanation: The first task of the support technician is to identify the problem. To do this, they ask the user what they were doing before the problem occurred and whether they made any changes to the laptop, for example an operating system update. After the problem is identified, they back up the data before they make any changes.
whyWrong: Backing up the data comes after the problem is identified and before any changes are made.
Researching the vendor’s website comes later, when you establish a theory of probable cause or a plan of action.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.1 question 3
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.1 (troubleshooting methodology). In 220-1201 the methodology is listed before Domain 5 as a best practice, not a numbered objective; tagged by the device in the question. The book stem said 'do first'; 'first' removed because both answers are parts of the same first step.

stem: A user complains that the cursor on her screen keeps drifting, and she cannot control it. What should be done to resolve this issue?
explanation: When the cursor on a touch screen keeps drifting, calibrate the screen so the digitizer matches touches to the right positions. Recalibration fixes most cursor drift problems.
whyWrong: A video cable fault causes a discolored or missing image, not a drifting cursor.
Nothing suggests a recent driver update, so rolling back the graphics driver is not indicated.
Changing the resolution only changes the size of items on the screen.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.4 question 9
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.4; tagged to current 5.4 cursor drift/touch calibration.

stem: A museum is experiencing issues with the touch-screen functionality on their Windows devices. Which of the following should be checked?
explanation: The display and touch settings in Windows include the options to calibrate the touch screen and to turn touch input on. Check them first when touch-screen input does not work correctly.
whyWrong: The battery status does not affect whether the touch screen responds.
The network connection has no effect on touch-screen input.
Keyboard settings do not control the touch screen.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.4 question 13
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.4; tagged to current 5.4 digitizer issues and touch calibration.

stem: What is the MOST LIKELY cause of a phone becoming excessively hot?
options: The phone is running resource-intensive apps
The phone is exposed to direct sunlight for a long time
The phone’s operating system needs an update
explanation: Excessive heat in a phone most likely comes from a defective battery. A battery that overheats can also swell, so stop using the phone and replace the battery.
whyWrong: Resource-intensive apps make a phone warm, but excessive heat more likely means a defective battery.
Direct sunlight can warm a phone, but it is a less likely cause of a phone that runs excessively hot.
An outdated operating system can cause performance problems but does not directly cause excessive heat.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.5 question 3
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.5 (mobile devices) = current 5.4.

stem: What is the BEST action to take if a phone has been exposed to liquid?
options: Immediately turn on the phone to check whether it is still functioning
Place the phone in a bag of rice for several hours to absorb the moisture
Use a hairdryer on low heat to dry the phone quickly
Take the phone to a professional repair service for assessment and cleaning
explanation: A phone with liquid damage needs a professional repair service to assess and clean it. Do not turn it on, because power can short-circuit the wet components.
whyWrong: Turning on a wet phone can short-circuit the components and cause more damage.
Rice does not fully dry the internal components, so it is not an effective fix.
A hairdryer adds heat that can damage the internal components further.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.5 question 4
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.5 (mobile devices) = current 5.4.

stem: A user complains that the computer is not connecting to the network. Which of the following should be done FIRST?
explanation: Check the obvious first: make sure the computer has a physical cabled connection to the network. Then try ipconfig, ping, and network driver updates.
whyWrong: Running ipconfig /all comes after you confirm the physical connection.
Pinging the router comes after you check the physical link.
Checking the network drivers is a later step, after the cable is confirmed.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: One of your customers received the error message “Network Path was Not Found” while trying to connect to a shared drive on the network at \\server1\datashare. Which of the following should you perform to resolve the issue? (Select two.)
options: Configure the network interface card to full duplex.
Use static IP addressing instead of DHCP.
explanation: The issue is most likely related to name resolution, which means DNS. Try resetting the TCP/IP stack with the netsh int ip reset command, or disable and then enable the Ethernet adapter. Flush the DNS cache with the ipconfig /flushdns command.
whyWrong: Full duplex lets the adapter send and receive at the same time, which does not fix a name resolution problem.
Disabling the Ethernet adapter alone leaves the computer with no connection; it must be enabled again.
A static IP address does not help when the problem is name-based and DNS is not resolving.
Disabling the local firewall weakens security and would not help, because the firewall normally does not block connections to a remote share.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: One of your customers no longer has access to a frequently accessed website. You ping another computer and the router on the network successfully. Which of the following should be done NEXT?
explanation: This is the concept of pinging outward: ping the localhost, then a computer, then the router, and then a domain name or website. If you can ping the website but the browser cannot get through, the browser might be compromised. If you cannot ping the website, check the IP configuration, because the DNS server address might be wrong.
whyWrong: Checking the IP configuration comes after a ping to the website fails, since the local pings already work.
Updating the OS is for a suspected compromise and comes after the connectivity tests.
Updating the antivirus software is for a suspected compromised browser, which the ping tests have not yet shown.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: A user moves a laptop from one office to another. The patch cable and the network adapter do not appear to be working properly at the new office. The cable is plugged in correctly and tests okay when checked with a patch tester. Which of the following should be done FIRST?
options: Check whether the port on the switch is enabled.
Replace the patch cable with a crossover cable.
Make sure the network adapter is compatible with the OS.
explanation: Some routers and switches can disable physical ports, which is a smart security measure, so first check that the switch port is enabled. Later, you can check whether the network adapter is compatible with the OS and update it if necessary.
whyWrong: Updating the adapter driver comes later, after you confirm that the switch port is enabled.
A crossover cable connects one computer directly to another, not a computer to a switch port.
The adapter worked at the old office, so OS compatibility is a later check.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: A computer is experiencing a problem in which the network connection alternates between a working state and nonworking state. It affects all applications. What is MOST LIKELY occurring in this scenario?
explanation: It is most likely port flapping (also called link flapping), where a communications link alternates between on and off states. Because the whole link goes up and down, every application is affected.
whyWrong: Jitter is an irregular time delay for particular packets, such as VoIP packets.
Network congestion means too much traffic on the network, which slows connections rather than turning the link on and off.
High latency means packets take longer to travel between systems, not that the connection stops and starts.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: A user is experiencing slow network transfer speeds. You suspect that the user’s system has too many open network connections to the Internet. Which of the following commands should you run to see which connections the user’s system has to the Internet?
explanation: Run netstat -a to see which connections the local computer currently has, including its connections to the Internet. Then advise the user to close unnecessary programs and limit the number of data streams.
whyWrong: The tracert command shows the route that packets take to a destination.
The ipconfig /release command releases the DHCP-obtained IP address.
The ipconfig /renew command requests a new DHCP-obtained IP address.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems, Cram Quiz question 6

stem: What is the FIRST thing you should check for when experiencing low RF and intermittent wireless connectivity issues?
options: The distance of the computer from the WAP
explanation: Check the distance of the computer from the WAP first, because a weak RF signal and intermittent connectivity often come from being too far away. Also consider the wireless channel that is in use, and check for external interference. If the equipment is old, the organization might need a new WAP.
whyWrong: An APIPA address (169.254.x.x) is a self-assigned address that shows a DHCP problem, not a weak RF signal.
QoS prioritizes important traffic on the router and does not improve the signal strength.
Outdated equipment is possible, but cables do not apply to a wireless signal problem, and distance is the simpler first check.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems, Cram Quiz question 7

stem: A desktop computer (named workstation22) can’t connect to the network. A network card was purchased without documentation or driver media (disc or thumb drive). Which of the following is the BEST way to install the network card driver?
options: Purchase the media online and install the drivers.
Run Windows Update to install the driver.
From the desktop computer (workstation22), download and install the driver.
Copy the driver to a flash drive and install it.
explanation: Go to another computer, download the driver from the manufacturer's website, copy it to a flash drive, and bring it back to the affected computer. The affected computer has no network connection, so it cannot download the driver itself.
whyWrong: Waiting for purchased driver media is slow and unnecessary when another computer can download the driver.
Windows Update needs a network connection, which this computer does not have, and it supplies Microsoft drivers rather than every vendor's drivers.
The computer cannot download anything because it has no network connection.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 19

stem: John is a PC technician for an organization that has a computer network with 12 computers. All the computers contain vital information, so they use static IP addresses (on the 192.168.50.0 network). John just finished troubleshooting a Windows computer that could not access the network. He ascertained (correctly) that the computer needed a new network card. He purchased a plug-and-play card and physically installed the card. He then turned on the computer and noted that the network card’s LED link was lit and that there was activity. He then rebooted the computer to Windows and documented the whole process. Later, his boss tells him that the user is complaining that there is no Internet access. Which step of the A+ troubleshooting methodology did John forget to perform?
options: Establish a theory of probable cause.
Test the theory to determine cause.
Establish a plan of action to resolve the problem.
explanation: John forgot to verify full system functionality. A new plug-and-play network card is set by default to obtain an IP address automatically, but this network uses static addresses on 192.168.50.0. Without a DHCP server, the computer self-assigns an APIPA (169.254.x.x) address and cannot reach the gateway or the Internet. John should have logged in and checked ipconfig /all, run a ping test, and tried websites before he closed the job.
whyWrong: John identified the problem correctly when he found that the computer could not access the network.
John established a correct theory that the network card had failed.
John tested the theory and confirmed that the computer needed a new network card.
John planned and carried out the fix when he bought and installed a new card.
John documented the whole process at the end.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 27
note: Asks for a step of the troubleshooting methodology, which the 220-1201 objectives list as a best practice but not as an objective; tagged to 5.5 for its network connectivity scenario.

stem: Four people share a connection to a SOHO router that connects to the Internet. When a single user starts streaming media over the Internet, browsing slows down for the rest of the users. Which setting should be configured to alleviate the problem?
explanation: Quality of service (QoS) controls the performance of user connections over the network, particularly connections to the Internet. On many SOHO routers, QoS can share bandwidth equally among all users or give priority to selected traffic, so one stream no longer slows everyone else.
whyWrong: DSL is a type of Internet connection over telephone lines, not a router setting that shares bandwidth.
A WAN is a network that spans a large geographic area and connects two or more LANs.
A VPN creates secure, tunneled connections over the Internet and does not share bandwidth among users.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 50
note: QoS is on the 220-1201 acronym list but is not named in an objective; tagged to 5.5 (slow network speeds).

stem: You are troubleshooting a user’s system that connects to the network and disconnects from the network in an alternating fashion. The system is connected via an Ethernet cable. Which of the following is the MOST LIKELY cause?
explanation: With port flapping, a communication link alternates between on and off states in a short period, which causes instability and intermittent connectivity. On a wired Ethernet connection, check the cable, the switch port, and the network adapter.
whyWrong: High latency means packets take longer than desired to reach a remote system, not that the link goes down.
Jitter is inconsistent latency, often noticed with VoIP.
External interference affects wireless connections, and this system uses an Ethernet cable.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 54

stem: You are servicing a small office’s network. One PC’s network adapter has a link light that is lit, but the PC can’t access internal network resources located on other PCs on the LAN. Which of the following is the MOST LIKELY cause of the issue?
explanation: An IP address conflict happens when two computers have the same IP address, usually when at least one was configured statically. The link light still works because the computer has a physical link to the switch, but communication at the IP layer fails. IP conflicts are most common in small networks that use static addresses.
whyWrong: High latency slows communication but does not stop the PC from reaching LAN resources.
Jitter is an irregular delay for some packets and does not block access to resources.
Limited connectivity means a system connects only some of the time, and it is a symptom rather than a cause.
An APIPA address is a symptom of a missing DHCP server rather than the cause of this problem.
With slow transfer speeds, the system would still reach internal resources eventually.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 66

stem: A user is unable to log in to their domain account despite entering the correct username and password. Which of the following should a technician check FIRST to identify the cause of the authentication failure?
options: Confirm the user’s password has not expired.
Ensure the workstation is not infected with malware.
Check if the workstation’s antivirus definitions are up to date.
Verify that the authentication server is reachable and the user’s account is not locked.
explanation: Authentication failures can come from an unreachable authentication server or from the account's status, such as locked or disabled. Check these first when the user is sure the credentials are correct, because either one blocks the login even with a valid password.
whyWrong: An expired password is possible, but a locked account or an unreachable server blocks the login even with a valid password, so check those first.
Malware is unlikely to cause an immediate domain authentication failure.
Out-of-date antivirus definitions do not stop a domain login.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 87

stem: A laptop user with an 802.11ax wireless network card just switched desk locations. In the new location, they say that their wireless drops connectivity intermittently and seems to have slow transfer speeds. Which of the following is MOST LIKELY to resolve these issues?
options: Run `ipconfig` to ensure that they are receiving the right IP address from the DHCP server.
Install a new WAP closer to their new desk.
Use a network monitor to ensure that there are no IP address conflicts.
explanation: Distance matters in wireless networks. Being too far away from an access point will result in a weaker signal, which can cause intermittent signal drops and poor performance. Moving closer to the wireless access point (WAP) or wireless router can help, as can installing additional WAPs or wireless routers.
whyWrong: Unless there are other issues, replacing a working NIC after a desk move is overkill.
The IP address from the DHCP server does not explain drops that began when the user moved farther away.
No error message was reported, so an IP address conflict is unlikely to be the cause.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 13

stem: While troubleshooting an intermittent Internet connectivity problem, you notice that port 443 on the router keeps opening and closing. What is this an example of?
explanation: The port quickly opening and closing is an example of port flapping. Port flapping makes the connection go up and down, which shows up as intermittent connectivity.
whyWrong: Jitter is variation in latency between packets, not a port going up and down.
High latency is a long delay on the network, not a port repeatedly opening and closing.
External interference could cause port problems, but it is not the name of this symptom.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 20

stem: What is a common symptom of a bad network cable?
explanation: If there are no link lights, you probably have a bad network cable. The link light comes on only when the NIC detects an electrical connection to the switch or other device at the far end.
whyWrong: Rapid blinking usually shows heavy network traffic on a working connection.
A solid link light shows a good connection, not a bad cable.
Steady blinking shows activity on a working link.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 19: Local Area Networking, Chapter Review question 7
note: All-in-One 11e (220-1101/1102) Ch. 19: link lights are not listed by name under 5.5; closest symptom is Limited connectivity.

stem: Ralph has installed a wireless network in his house, placing the wireless access point in the kitchen, a centralized location. The Wi-Fi works fine in the living room and dining room but goes out almost completely in the bedroom. What is MOST LIKELY the problem?
options: The SSID overlapping with a neighbor’s SSID
explanation: Watch out for microwave ovens, refrigerators, and pipes in the walls. Metal objects like these can block or interfere with a Wi-Fi signal and create dead spots in some rooms.
whyWrong: An antenna problem would weaken the signal everywhere, not only in one room.
The default SSID is a security concern but does not affect signal strength.
An overlapping neighbor's network would cause interference in all rooms, not only the bedroom.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 20: Wireless Networking, Chapter Review question 10

stem:
A laptop user tries to surf the internet but finds they have no connectivity. Running the ipconfig /all command produces the following output:
IPv4 Address. . . . . . . . . . . : 169.254.10.1
Subnet Mask . . . . . . . . . . . : 255.255.0.0
Default Gateway . . . . . . . . . :
DHCP Enabled . . . . . . . . . . . : Yes
Which of the following is the source of this problem?
explanation: An address in the 169.254.x.x range is an Automatic Private IP Address (APIPA). A DHCP client gives itself one only when it cannot get an address from the DHCP server, for example because of a network problem or because the server has no free addresses. The APIPA address gives only limited connectivity, with no internet access.
whyWrong: DNS resolves host names to IP addresses; a DNS problem would not cause an APIPA address.
NetBIOS is a legacy Microsoft name resolution protocol and has nothing to do with address assignment.
With a static IP address, the output would show DHCP Enabled as No.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.1 question 8
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.1; limited connectivity with an APIPA address is current 5.5 (also 2.6 APIPA).

stem: What action should be taken to resolve limited or no connectivity for a wireless client in a network due to an IP address issue?
options: Release and renew the IP address
Flush the DNS cache on the computer
explanation: When a wireless client has limited or no connectivity because of an IP address problem, release its current IP address and request a new one from the network’s DHCP server. On Windows, use ipconfig /release and ipconfig /renew.
whyWrong: The problem is the IP address, not the network card driver.
Changing the wireless channel does not give the client a valid IP address.
Flushing the DNS cache fixes name resolution problems, not an invalid IP address.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.7 question 3
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.7 (network troubleshooting) = current 5.5.

stem: In a wireless network setup with two routers, what can be done to avoid high latency issues?
options: Separate wireless channels, each with its own IP address range
explanation: Configure the two routers on different, non-overlapping channels, each with its own IP address range. This minimizes interference between them and reduces latency.
whyWrong: Channel bonding widens the channel, which increases interference between the two routers and can worsen latency.
Wired connections avoid wireless latency, but the setup is meant to be a wireless network.
QoS prioritizes traffic but does not remove the interference that causes the latency.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.7 question 5
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.7 (network troubleshooting) = current 5.5.

stem: What is a possible solution to address a wireless connection that keeps dropping in an office environment?
explanation: Relocating the wireless router to a central location improves the signal coverage and reduces interference from other devices. This reduces the connection drops.
whyWrong: More internet bandwidth does not fix a weak or interrupted wireless signal.
Turning off all other wireless devices is rarely possible in an office.
Changing the encryption method affects security, not signal drops.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.7 question 7
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.7 (network troubleshooting) = current 5.5.

stem: What could be a potential cause of poor Voice over Internet Protocol ( VoIP) quality?
explanation: Poor VoIP quality occurs when there is not enough bandwidth for the voice data, which leads to delay, jitter, and dropped audio. QoS can give voice traffic priority.
whyWrong: Outdated hardware is not directly linked to poor call quality across the network.
A low battery does not affect the quality of VoIP audio.
Low microphone sensitivity makes the voice quiet but does not cause the network quality problems of VoIP.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.7 question 9
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.7 (network troubleshooting) = current 5.5.

stem: How can a paper jam be resolved? (Select all that apply.)
options: Use the right type of paper.
Check for and replace damaged rollers.
explanation: A paper jam can happen because paper is stuck in the paper path, the paper is too thick or the wrong type, or the rollers are damaged. Clear the paper path, use the right type of paper, and replace damaged rollers.
whyWrong: Checking the operator control panel (OCP) may tell you why the jam happened, but it does not resolve it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 28: Troubleshooting Printers, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: A technician is troubleshooting finishing issues with the company laser printer. Which of the following actions should the tech perform? (Select all that apply.)
options: Clean the filament nozzle and platform (print bed).
Make sure the staple cartridge is full and free of jams.
Ensure that the hole punch tray is not full.
Ensure that the proper paper tray is specified in the printer settings.
explanation: For finishing issues such as stapling and hole punching, check the staple cartridge, the hole punch tray, the tray settings, and the paper orientation. An empty or jammed staple cartridge or a full hole punch tray stops the finisher.
whyWrong: Cleaning the filament nozzle and print bed is maintenance for a 3D printer, not a laser printer.
The toner cartridge matters for printing but not for finishing processes such as stapling and hole punching.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 28: Troubleshooting Printers, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: One of your customers is connected to a standalone printer. The customer gets an “out of memory” error when printing large graphic files. What should you do?
options: Upgrade the storage drive on the computer.
Upgrade the RAM on the printer.
Upgrade the RAM on the computer.
explanation: Upgrade the RAM on the printer, because large graphics files need a lot of memory in both the PC and the printer. If the PC can send the file to the printer, it has enough RAM and drive space, so the shortfall is in the printer.
whyWrong: The PC already sent the file, so its storage drive space is not the shortfall.
The PC's own memory was enough to send the file; the error comes from the printer.
Printer drivers do not cause an “out of memory” error on the printer.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 28: Troubleshooting Printers, Cram Quiz question 5
note: An out-of-memory error is not a named 5.6 symptom; tagged to the closest topic, jobs that stay pending in the queue.

stem: What should you do FIRST when removing a paper jam?
options: Open all the doors of the printer.
explanation: Turn off the printer before you start working inside it, and make sure it is unplugged before you put your hands inside. Taking it offline is not enough, because the printer still has power and hot or moving parts.
whyWrong: Taking the printer offline stops jobs but leaves it powered, which is not safe for reaching inside.
Clearing the print queue does not make it safe to remove a jammed sheet.
Open the doors only after the printer is turned off and unplugged.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 28: Troubleshooting Printers, Cram Quiz question 6

stem: Which is the faster option for spooling documents?
options: Start printing after last page is spooled
Start printing after the separator page
explanation: Start printing immediately is faster than Start printing after last page is spooled, because printing begins while the rest of the job is still spooling. Both options are spooling settings on the Advanced tab of the printer's properties in Windows.
whyWrong: Print directly to the printer bypasses the spooling feature altogether.
Start printing after last page is spooled waits for the whole job, so printing starts later.
There is no spooling option called Start printing after the separator page.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 28: Troubleshooting Printers, Cram Quiz question 8
note: Spooling options are not a named 5.6 symptom; tagged to the closest topic, jobs pending in the queue.

stem: How can you immediately stop the Print Spooler service? (Select the three best answers.)
options: Type sc config spooler start= disabled in the Command Prompt.
Type net stop spooler in the Command Prompt.
Open the Services console window, right-click Print Spooler, and select Stop.
Open the Task Manager, click the Services tab, right-click Spooler, and select Stop.
explanation: To stop the Print Spooler service immediately, run net stop spooler (or sc stop spooler) in the Command Prompt. You can also stop it in the Services console, where it is listed as Print Spooler, or on the Services tab of Task Manager, where it is listed as Spooler.
whyWrong: Start printing immediately is a spooling option in the printer properties and does not stop the service.
The sc config spooler start= disabled command changes the startup type for the next boot but does not stop the running service.
Print directly to the printer bypasses spooling for that printer but leaves the service running.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 28: Troubleshooting Printers, Cram Quiz question 9

stem: One of your coworkers has opened a trouble ticket concerning paper jams on a laser printer. The paper jams have become more frequent as of late. You attempt to re-create the problem and then check the printer log for more information. Which of the following are the MOST LIKELY solutions to the problem? (Select the two best answers.)
options: Clean and inspect the entire paper path.
