Clean the fuser roller and verify fuser operation.
Clean and replace the paper out sensor.
Use a printer maintenance kit to replace parts.
Replace the paper exit assembly switch.
Clean and inspect the print drum.
explanation: Clean and inspect the entire paper path first; it costs nothing, and clearing out stuck paper often solves the problem. Also use the correct printer maintenance kit to replace worn parts, which should be installed every 100,000 to 200,000 pages depending on the printer. Worn parts often lead to paper jams, especially when the problem has been getting worse.
whyWrong: Paper jams don't usually start in the fusing assembly, although it is possible.
Replacing the paper out sensor is uncommon and does not address worn feed parts.
Replacing a paper exit assembly switch is uncommon and is not a likely fix for growing jams.
Print drum problems cause streaks, marks, and ghosting rather than paper jams, and the drum is usually replaced with the toner cartridge.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 8

stem: A client is having a problem printing a specific type of document. The main network printer operator control panel (OCP) shows that the printer is online and that there are no errors. No other users are having issues printing to that printer. You ask the person to send the same document to another printer, and the document prints fine. Which of the following should you do FIRST when troubleshooting this problem?
options: Stop and start the print spooler service.
Stop and start the print server queues and have the user resend the document.
Verify that the user is sending the document to the correct printer queue.
Have all users send the same document to the correct printer queue.
explanation: Verify that the user is sending the document to the correct printer queue. When a network has several printers, it is easy to mistake one printer name for another. The printer's operator control panel (OCP) shows no errors and other users print fine, so the problem is on the user's side.
whyWrong: The user can print the same document to other printers, so the user's print spooler is working.
Restarting the print server queues disrupts other users and does not help a user who sends jobs to the wrong queue.
Other users already print to that printer, so asking everyone to send the document wastes their time.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 18

stem: Your office printer was working earlier in the day but is no longer printing any documents. Preexisting workstations are manually configured to print to the printer directly over the network. You begin troubleshooting the problem and determine that the printer is still visible when browsing the network directory. You also verify, at the physical printer, that the printer can print test pages successfully. Which of the following is the MOST LIKELY cause of the problem?
options: Two users sent print jobs at the same time, and a collision occurred.
The printer’s IP address has changed.
The message “perform printer maintenance” is displayed on the printer’s display panel.
explanation: The printer's IP address has most likely changed. The workstations were manually configured to print to the printer, most likely by IP address, so an address change makes their print jobs fail. The printer still shows in the network directory, which usually searches by name, and it prints test pages, so the printer itself works. Configure a static IP address at the printer to prevent this.
whyWrong: Restarting the print spooler fixes hung spooling issues; it does not stop a printer from working.
Print jobs cannot collide; they are placed in a queue at the printer or the print server.
A maintenance message does not usually stop printing, though you should attend to it right away.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 25

stem: You are troubleshooting a printer. Which of the following are common symptoms of printer failure or other printer issues? (Select the three best answers.)
options: Vertical lines down the printed pages
Failure to document screw and cable locations
explanation: Vertical lines down the page, garbled print, and faded print are common printer symptoms. Vertical lines usually point to a print drum issue, fixed by replacing the toner cartridge or calibrating an inkjet. Garbled print often comes from an incorrect driver, so use the exact driver for the printer model and the OS. For faded print, replace the ink or toner, clean the inkjet head, and check the fuser.
whyWrong: Failing to document screw and cable locations can make reassembly hard, but it is a possible cause of trouble, not a symptom.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 61

stem: A user reports that nothing is printing and multiple jobs are stuck in the queue. Canceling the jobs does not work. What is the NEXT best step a technician should take to clear the print queue?
options: Reboot the printer and the computer.
Change the printer’s default paper tray.
Lower the printer’s print quality setting.
Stop and restart the print spooler service.
explanation: When jobs are stuck and cannot be cleared through the interface, the most effective way to reset the queue is to stop and restart the print spooler service. This also lets the technician clear the spool folder and remove any corrupted jobs.
whyWrong: Rebooting may fix basic communication issues, but it often does not clear a queue stuck because of a malfunctioning spooler.
The default paper tray setting addresses paper selection, not stuck jobs.
The print quality setting affects speed and clarity, not stalled jobs in the queue.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 88

stem: You have just installed a new printer, but it prints only garbled text. Which of the following is MOST LIKELY the problem?
explanation: If a printer is using out-of-date or incorrect printer drivers, the printer may produce pages of garbled text. The solution is to ensure that the most recent printer drivers are downloaded from the manufacturer's website.
whyWrong: A wrong IP address would stop jobs from reaching the printer rather than print garbled text.
A worn printhead causes faded or streaked output, not garbled characters.
An unsupported printer would usually fail to install or print rather than print garbled text.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Review Questions question 14

stem: Users are complaining that their print jobs are not printing. You open the print queue and see 50 jobs lined up. The printer is connected properly and online. What should you do?
options: Open the Printer Troubleshooting utility on the printing device and have it diagnose the problem.
Stop and restart the print spooler.
explanation: If print jobs are seemingly getting stuck in the printer queue, you should stop and restart the print spooler service. Restarting the spooler clears the stalled job so the queue can move again.
whyWrong: There is no Printer Troubleshooting utility on the physical printer, though Windows has a Printer troubleshooter.
Deleting and reinstalling the printer is not necessary when restarting the spooler clears the queue.
Reinstalling Windows is far more than a stuck print queue needs.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 4

stem: Your laser printer keeps printing vertical black lines on its output pages. What is the MOST LIKELY cause of the problem?
options: There is a groove or scratch in the EP drum.
The EP drum-cleaning blade is broken.
The printer is low on toner.
The transfer corona wire is not working properly.
explanation: The most likely cause is a groove or a scratch in the EP drum. Toner is collecting in that groove or scratch, and then it is being deposited onto the page.
whyWrong: A broken drum-cleaning blade would result in unreadable images with too much toner, not one vertical line.
Low toner would cause faded images rather than black lines.
A bad transfer corona wire would cause blank images.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 7

stem: You have an inkjet printer. Recently, papers are being printed with excessive amounts of ink, and the ink is smearing. What is the MOST LIKELY cause of the problem?
options: Too much humidity in the air
explanation: If an ink cartridge is faulty or develops a hole, it can release excessive amounts of ink, which will lead to smearing. The solution is to replace the ink cartridge.
whyWrong: A corrupted print driver would result in printing garbage characters, not extra ink.
Inkjet printers do not have a fuser; fusers are found in laser printers.
Excessive humidity may cause smearing, but it wouldn't cause too much ink to be released.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 9
note: Ink smearing is not a listed 220-1201 5.6 symptom; tagged with the closest print-quality symptom (speckling).

stem: When you print documents on your laser printer, you see residue from previous images on the output. Which two things are the MOST LIKELY causes of this problem? (Choose two.)
explanation: Seeing images from previous print jobs is a phenomenon called ghosting (or ghost images). It's most likely due to a bad erasure lamp or a broken cleaning blade, which leave charge or toner from the last image on the drum.
whyWrong: A faulty transfer corona wire would most likely produce blank pages.
An overheating printer will not necessarily leave residue behind.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 10

stem: You support an old impact printer at work. When the printer prints, there is always a blank horizontal line in the middle of each line of output. What is the MOST LIKELY cause of the problem?
options: The print ribbon is old and needs to be replaced.
The print ribbon is not advancing properly.
The printhead needs to be replaced.
The wrong print driver is installed.
explanation: If there is a consistent blank space, it likely means that a pin is not firing properly and the printhead needs to be replaced. Each pin of a dot-matrix printhead prints one row of dots, so a dead pin leaves the same gap in every line.
whyWrong: An old print ribbon would give consistently faded printing, not one blank line.
A ribbon that is not advancing properly would give light and dark printing.
The wrong print driver would produce garbage characters.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 11
note: A missing line from a dead printhead pin; the closest 220-1201 5.6 symptom is lines on the printed pages.

stem: When printing to a laser printer, all you get is random characters on the page. What is the FIRST thing to try?
options: Replace the formatter board in the laser printer.
Perform calibration to align the printheads.
explanation: If the printer is printing garbled output, the most likely cause of the problem is the print driver. Make sure it's the correct driver for the printer. Then, either update the driver, or remove the printer from the OS and reinstall it to get a new driver.
whyWrong: The formatter board could cause garbled output, but checking the driver is far easier and comes first.
If the printer cable were not seated properly, there likely would be no output at all.
Laser printers do not have printheads to align.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 14

stem: When an inkjet printer is printing jobs, it's making a squealing sound. What is MOST LIKELY causing this problem?
options: The paper caliper is too thick
explanation: Squealing or grinding noises are made by components that have moving parts. In this case, it's possibly a motor such as the stepper motor.
whyWrong: Ink cartridges shouldn't be refilled, but a refilled cartridge does not make a squealing sound.
Paper thickness won't cause a squealing sound.
A failing formatter board is electronic and makes no squealing noise.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 17

stem: An inkjet printer consistently feeds two or three pieces of paper for every page it's supposed to print. Which of the following could be the cause of the problem? (Choose two.)
options: The paper moisture content is too high.
The tension in the pickup tray needs to be adjusted.
The printer is using the incorrect tray setting.
The printer is using the incorrect page orientation.
The printer is experiencing finishing issues.
explanation: Paper that is too damp, possibly due to high humidity, can become sticky, making the printer grab more than one sheet at a time. It could also be a tension issue in the paper pickup mechanism.
whyWrong: Tray settings affect the size or type of paper, such as envelopes, not how many sheets are picked up.
Page orientation affects the width and height of the output, not paper feeding.
Finishing issues are related to stapling or hole punching, not paper pickup.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 19

stem: A standalone printer prints a test page just fine, but it makes gobbledygook out of your term paper. What’s probably wrong?
explanation: The application (software) that is trying to print is probably configured incorrectly. Because the test page prints fine, the printer hardware works, and the problem is in the software or driver settings.
whyWrong: A printer out of toner would print faded or blank test pages too.
A fuser error would affect the test page as well.
The test page proves the printer interface is working.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 26: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Chapter Review question 8

stem: Which tool would help you determine why a print job didn’t print?
explanation: The print spooler can help you determine why a print job did not print. It holds the queue of print jobs and shows their status, such as paused, error, or stuck.
whyWrong: A printer driver translates print jobs for the printer but does not show their status.
Printer setup is not a tool that shows why a job failed.
System setup (the firmware setup utility) does not manage print jobs.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 26: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Chapter Review question 10

stem: What could be the issue if printed documents have poor print quality? (Choose two)
options: The printer is low on ink or toner
The printer driver needs to be updated
explanation: Low ink or toner causes faded or streaky prints. Low-quality paper also lowers print quality, causing smudges, bleeding ink, or a lack of sharpness.
whyWrong: An outdated driver more often causes garbled print than poor print quality.
Wrong settings can lower quality, but low supplies and poor paper are the usual causes.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.6 question 10
note: Old objective 220-1101 3.6 (printers and MFDs).

stem: What could be the issue if a printed document is coming out landscape instead of portrait? How can we resolve this issue?
options: The wrong printer settings are selected
The printer’s ink or toner is low
explanation: If the wrong orientation is selected in the printer settings or the application, the document prints in landscape instead of portrait. Select portrait orientation and print again.
whyWrong: An outdated driver can cause garbled print, but it does not choose the page orientation.
Low ink or toner causes faded prints, not a wrong orientation.
A wrong paper size changes the page size, not necessarily the orientation.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.7 question 3
note: Old objective 220-1101 3.7 (printer maintenance).

stem: A systems administrator is given a ticket by the help desk to deal with the chief executive officer’s printer. Their secretary said that it will not print, a light is flashing, and they think the printer paper is the issue. What should the systems administrator do FIRST?
options: Verify the printer’s full system functionality
Test a theory to determine the cause of the printer issue
Identify the problem with the printer
Establish a plan of action to resolve the email server issue
explanation: The first stage of the troubleshooting methodology is to identify the problem with the printer, without accepting the solution that a user suggests. After this, you establish a theory of probable cause, test the theory, and then establish a plan of action.
whyWrong: Verifying full system functionality comes near the end of the process, after the fix is in place.
You test a theory only after you have identified the problem and established a theory of probable cause.
A plan of action comes after the cause is known, and the ticket is about a printer, not an email server.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.1 question 1
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.1 (troubleshooting methodology). In 220-1201 the methodology is listed before Domain 5 as a best practice, not a numbered objective; tagged by the device in the question.

stem: What could be the potential cause of print quality issues, including marks on the printing paper? ( Choose two)
options: The printer’s firmware requires an update
The printer’s drum unit is damaged
The printer has dirty feed rollers
The printer’s ink cartridges are low on ink
explanation: Marks on printed pages come from a damaged drum unit, which transfers the same flaw to each page, or from dirty feed rollers, which leave marks as they move the paper. Replace the drum or clean the rollers.
whyWrong: Firmware updates do not usually affect print quality or marks on the paper.
Low ink gives faded or missing print, not marks on the paper.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.6 question 4
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.6 (printers).

stem: When paper fails to feed properly in a printer, what is the MOST LIKELY cause?
options: The paper is too thick for the printer
The printer driver needs to be updated
The ink cartridges are low on ink
explanation: Printers have limits on paper weight and thickness, and paper that is too thick for the printer fails to feed. Check the printer specifications and use supported paper.
whyWrong: With an empty tray, the printer reports that it is out of paper rather than misfeeding.
An outdated driver can cause print errors, but not problems with the paper feed.
Low ink affects print quality, not how paper is fed.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.6 question 5
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.6 (printers).

stem: What is the MOST LIKELY cause of a paper jam in a printer?
options: The paper is wrinkled or folded
There are obstructions in the paper path
The ink cartridges are low on ink
explanation: Obstructions in the paper path, such as small pieces of torn paper or debris, are the most likely cause of paper jams. Remove them carefully and check the path before printing again.
whyWrong: An empty tray stops the printer from feeding paper, but it does not cause a jam.
Wrinkled or folded paper can jam, but it is a less likely cause than an obstruction in the paper path.
Low ink does not cause paper jams.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.6 question 6
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.6 (printers).

stem: A user is experiencing gaps in the printed labels from their label printer. What is the MOST LIKELY cause of this issue?
options: Low ink or toner levels in the printer
A paper jam inside the printer
explanation: Gaps on printed labels are typically caused by incorrect label alignment or positioning, so the printer prints across the gap between labels. Calibrate the label printer and check the label size settings.
whyWrong: Gaps on labels are not typically caused by low ink or toner, and many label printers are thermal printers that use neither.
A paper jam stops the labels from feeding, rather than leaving regular gaps in the print.
Outdated drivers or firmware can cause various problems, but gaps on labels are usually an alignment issue.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.6 question 14
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.6 (printers). Tagged to current 5.6 incorrect page orientation (closest topic for label position).

stem: What could be the cause of a laser printer producing a ghost image on the printed page?
options: A dirty or damaged imaging drum
A loose connection between the printer and the computer
explanation: If the imaging drum is not cleaned properly or is damaged, it keeps remnants of the previous image. A faint duplicate (ghost) image then appears on the following printouts.
whyWrong: A low fuser temperature makes toner smear or rub off; it does not cause ghost images.
Low toner gives faded or light prints, not a duplicate image.
A loose connection causes communication errors or stops jobs, not ghost images.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.6 question 15
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.6 (printers).

stem: A technician is troubleshooting an issue where lines appear down copied pages, but the printed pages sent directly to the copier render as intended. What is the MOST LIKELY cause of this issue?
explanation: Lines appear only on copied pages, while pages printed directly render as intended, so the fault is in the scanning part of the copier. Damaged or dirty scanning glass puts lines on every copy but does not affect print jobs.
whyWrong: A clogged print head would affect both copied and directly printed pages.
An overheated fuser would affect both copied and directly printed pages.
An incompatible toner would affect printed pages as well as copies.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.6 question 17
note: Book answer D (incompatible toner) corrected: toner is used for both copies and prints, so a fault only on copies points to the scanning glass. Old 220-1101 objective 5.6 (printers).

stem: A laser printer is consistently printing garbled text instead of clear, readable text. What is the MOST LIKELY cause of this issue?
options: Low ink or toner levels in the printer
Incorrect printer settings or font compatibility
explanation: Garbled text is most likely caused by outdated or incorrect printer drivers or firmware, so the printer cannot interpret the print job correctly. Updating the drivers or firmware to the latest version can resolve the issue.
whyWrong: Low toner gives faded prints or incomplete text, not garbled text.
Damaged cables can cause printing problems, but a driver problem is the more likely cause of consistent garbled text.
Incorrect settings or fonts can cause print issues, but consistently garbled text more likely comes from the drivers or firmware.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.6 question 18
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.6 (printers).

stem: A laser printer consistently prints a line from the top of the page down to the bottom on every sheet. What is the MOST LIKELY cause of this issue?
options: Low ink or toner levels in the printer
Dust or debris on the imaging drum
explanation: Dust or debris on the imaging drum, or a scratch on it, puts a consistent line from the top to the bottom of every sheet. Cleaning or replacing the imaging drum usually resolves the issue.
whyWrong: Low toner gives faded prints or incomplete text, not one consistent line.
A faulty paper feed causes jams or skewed pages, not a single line down every page.
Drivers or firmware do not cause a consistent vertical line on every page.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.6 question 20
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.6 (printers).

stem: A printer is producing a grinding noise during printing. What is the MOST LIKELY cause of this issue?
options: Low ink or toner levels in the printer
A paper jam or obstruction in the printer
explanation: A grinding noise during printing is commonly caused by a paper jam or an obstruction in the printer, or by worn gears. Turn off the printer and check the paper path.
whyWrong: Low toner or ink does not make the printer grind.
Drivers and firmware do not cause mechanical noises.
A network problem stops jobs from reaching the printer; it does not make a grinding noise.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.6 question 21
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.6 (printers).

stem: A laser printer shows that its second paper tray is not recognized, so jobs for that tray do not print. What should the technician do FIRST?
options: Check that the tray is fully inserted and aligned with the printer's guides
explanation: A tray that is not recognized is often just not seated: start by checking that it is securely installed and aligned with the guides. If that does not help, check the tray's paper size settings, then the firmware and driver, and finally the tray's sensor.
whyWrong: The fuser bonds toner to the paper and has nothing to do with tray detection.
A firmware update can help, but it comes after the quick physical check.
Replacing a sensor is the last step, after the simple checks fail.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 28: Troubleshooting Printers

stem: After a new paper tray is added to a printer, the tray is seated correctly but print jobs still cannot use it. The printer's control panel lists the tray as disabled. What is the MOST LIKELY fix?
options: Enable and configure the tray in the printer settings
explanation: A tray that is disabled or not configured in the printer's settings cannot be used, even when it is installed correctly. Enable it and set its paper size and type in the control panel or printer software.
whyWrong: Toner affects print quality, not whether a tray is recognized.
Dirty pickup rollers cause misfeeds, not a disabled tray.
The tray setting is in the printer, so reinstalling the operating system does not change it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 28: Troubleshooting Printers

stem: A laser printer often pulls several sheets at once. The paper is the right weight. What is the MOST LIKELY cause?
explanation: The separation pad lets only one sheet through at a time. When it wears and loses traction, the printer pulls several sheets together, so check or replace the pad; paper that is too thin can cause the same problem.
whyWrong: An empty toner cartridge gives faded or blank pages, not misfeeds.
A failed fuser leaves toner that smears or rubs off.
A wrong driver causes garbled output, not a mechanical misfeed.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 28: Troubleshooting Printers

stem: A multifunction printer prints the pages of a job but does not staple them. Which of the following should the technician check? (Choose two.)
options: The finishing (staple) setting for the job
explanation: Finishing issues such as missing staples or holes come from the finisher: check the staple cartridge (or the hole punch tray) and the finishing and tray settings of the job. Toner and the fuser affect the printed image, not stapling.
whyWrong: The fuser bonds toner to the paper and does not affect stapling.
The toner level affects print darkness, not finishing.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 28: Troubleshooting Printers
